name: jsonata

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: A [JSONata expression](https://docs.jsonata.org/expressions). Typically a SQL literal — when it's constant the extension parses it once and reuses the compiled program across every row.

parameters.name: json_data
parameters.description: The JSON value the expression is evaluated against. Any DuckDB [`JSON`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions.html) value — column, literal, or function result.

parameters.name: bindings
parameters.description: Optional. JSON object whose keys become `$variable` names accessible inside the expression. Use it to parameterize a static expression with per-query values (thresholds, ids, dates).

returns: Result of evaluating the expression — typed as [`JSON`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions.html). Cast (`::VARCHAR`, `::DOUBLE`, `::JSON[]`) or `unnest` downstream depending on what the expression returns.
description:
Evaluates a [JSONata](https://jsonata.org/) expression against a JSON document and returns the result as `JSON`.

JSONata is a [lightweight query and transformation language for JSON](https://docs.jsonata.org/overview), modelled on XPath. The expression can be a [path traversal](https://docs.jsonata.org/path-operators), an [array predicate filter](https://docs.jsonata.org/predicate), an [object-construction](https://docs.jsonata.org/construction) literal that reshapes the input, or any combination — all in one string.

Two arities:

- `jsonata(expression, json_data)` — the common form.
- `jsonata(expression, json_data, bindings)` — passes a `bindings` JSON object whose keys become `$variable` names inside the expression. Useful when the expression is a SQL constant but the parameters are per-query (e.g. a threshold lifted from a [SQL variable](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/set#variables)).

When `expression` is a SQL constant — the typical case — it's parsed once and the compiled program is reused per row. Per-row cost is JSON walk + apply.

The full JSONata language reference, including [string functions](https://docs.jsonata.org/string-functions), [numeric functions](https://docs.jsonata.org/numeric-functions), [aggregation](https://docs.jsonata.org/aggregation-functions), [higher-order functions](https://docs.jsonata.org/higher-order-functions), [sorting and grouping](https://docs.jsonata.org/sorting-grouping), and [programming constructs](https://docs.jsonata.org/programming), applies. The interactive [JSONata exerciser](https://try.jsonata.org/) is the fastest way to iterate on an expression before pasting it into SQL.
